title: Spectral peak picking — Audio Fingerprint Search
description: Fingerprinting starts from a spectrogram: time on one axis, frequency on the other, energy as brightness. Peak picking keeps only local energy maxima, the 'constellation' of the recording. Peaks survive compression and background noise far better than raw waveforms.

title: Peak-pair hashing — Audio Fingerprint Search
description: Each fingerprint hash combines two peaks: their frequencies and the time between them. Pairing makes hashes translation-invariant in time: a clip starting anywhere still matches. The fanout parameter bounds how many partners each peak pairs with, controlling hash count.
provenance: Public methodology — standard computer-science technique documented in the technical literature; fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Time-offset voting — Audio Fingerprint Search
description: Matching hashes vote for the time offset between query and reference; the true song accumulates a sharp peak. Random collisions scatter votes uniformly, so the offset histogram separates signal from noise. This is how a 10-second phone recording identifies a song in a million-track catalog.
provenance: Public methodology — standard computer-science technique documented in the technical literature; fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Robustness to noise — Audio Fingerprint Search
description: Peak constellations ignore everything below the local-maximum threshold, discarding crowd noise and chatter. Only the strongest time-frequency landmarks participate, so bar-room recordings still identify. Robustness is measured by identification rate at decreasing signal-to-noise ratios.

title: Landmark density control — Audio Fingerprint Search
description: Denser peaks mean more hashes and better recall but bigger indexes; sparser peaks save space but risk misses. Systems tune peak density per frequency band, keeping more landmarks where music is most distinctive. Density control is the main knob trading index size against identification accuracy.

title: Chromaprint-style fingerprints — Audio Fingerprint Search
description: Chromaprint computes 32-bit sub-fingerprints per short window from spectral band energies. Consecutive sub-fingerprints form the full fingerprint, compared with bit-error-tolerant matching. It is the open algorithm behind acoustic music identification tools.

title: Handling pitch and tempo shifts — Audio Fingerprint Search
description: Cover versions change key and tempo; shift-tolerant matchers compare relative intervals instead of absolute frequencies. Dynamic time warping aligns sequences stretched or compressed in time. Interval-based fingerprints identify melodies across arrangements.

title: Fingerprint index sharding — Audio Fingerprint Search
description: Hash-to-song postings lists are sharded by hash value so queries fan out across machines. Each shard returns candidate (song, offset) votes that a coordinator merges. Sharding keeps per-query latency flat as the catalog grows to tens of millions.

title: Query-by-humming — Audio Fingerprint Search
description: Humming queries extract a pitch contour and match it against melody databases with sequence alignment. Contour matching tolerates wrong absolute pitch but punishes wrong intervals. It turns 'that tune stuck in my head' into a searchable query.

title: Duplicate audio detection — Audio Fingerprint Search

title: Speech versus music separation — Audio Fingerprint Search
